cells.value: High Concentrations
Moderate Concentrations
Definition
Gas streams over 24% H₂S by volume. Liquid streams over 4.0 psia H₂S vapor pressure.
Gas streams 1-24% H₂S by volume. Liquid streams, 0.05-4.0 psia H₂S vapor pressure.
Piping

1. Q Class preferred. N Class acceptable with 100% radiography.
2. Stress relieve if required by Code or service conditions.

1. Use H or N Classes.
2. Stress relieve if required by Code or service conditions.
Pressure Vessels & Heat Exchangers

1. Avoid nozzles smaller than NPS 2.
2. Use ANSI Class 300 flanges. Otherwise the same as for moderate H₂S concentrations.
3. Use NPS 2 piping for connections to vessels and piping.
4. Stress relieve if required by Code or service conditions.

1. Design to ASME Sec. VIII and RP 19.
2. Generally conform to PVM-EG-2560 or EXH-EG-2583.
3. Hydrotest and random X-ray.
4. Stress relieve if required by Code requirements.
5. Minimize number of connections; use confined gaskets.
Pumps

1. Avoid if possible.
2. Otherwise the same as for moderate H₂S concentrations.

1. Select high quality pump with low shaft deflection.
2. Use mechanical seals with non-H₂S seal flush.
3. Use steel, not cast iron for pressure containing parts. Avoid copper alloys.
Compressors

1. Avoid if possible.
2. Otherwise the same as for moderate H₂S concentrations.

1. Vent seals to a safe location.
2. Consult specialist.
Instruments

1. Avoid instrument connections on vessels and use NPS 2 minimum instrument bridles.
2. Avoid gage glasses in high pressure H₂S service.
3. Otherwise the same as for moderate H₂S concentrations.

1. Use NPS ¾ minimum piping connections to vessels and piping.
2. Use root valves to permit isolation of instruments.
3. Use restrictor fittings at root valves.
4. Use ½ inch stainless steel tubing for instrument leads.
5. Minimize small piping and tubing.
